title: Turn-ON  fluorescence detection of Cu 2+  ions using a triphenylamine-adorned chromene-based molecular ensemble for environmental monitoring and plant tissue imaging
content: The development of highly sensitive and selective turn-ON fluorescent molecular probes for copper(ii) (Cu2+) ion detection is significant owing to the crucial role of copper in biological and environmental conditions. Herein, a new chromene-derived fluorogenic probe, 2-amino-4-(4-(diphenylamino)phenyl)-7-hydroxy-4H-chromene-3-carbonitrile (TPA-HC), was synthesized via a simple one-pot synthesis and comprehensively characterized by FT-IR spectroscopy, 1H and 13C NMR, HR-MS, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction analyses. Owing to the combination of the chromene and electron-donating triphenylamine (TPA) unit, TPA-HC exhibits tuneable fluorescence and demonstrates a highly selective detection toward Cu2+ ions over various competing metal ions. Upon Cu2+ coordination to TPA-HC, the fluorescence intensity is enhanced by ∼12-folds with an ultra-low limit of detection (LOD) of ∼561 pM with a good linear response. Detailed mechanistic investigations (Job's plot, 1H NMR, and HR-MS) confirmed the formation of a stable 1 : 1 TPA-HC–Cu2+ complex, which is responsible for the observed fluorescence enhancement. The practical applicability of TPA-HC was successfully demonstrated through the determination of Cu2+ ions in lake, Milli-Q and tap water samples, exhibiting satisfactory recoveries (76–122%) and detection in picomolar levels. Furthermore, a smartphone-assisted RGB colour recognition platform enabled the rapid qualitative and quantitative analysis of Cu2+ ions, while fluorescence imaging in pea root tissues demonstrated the capability of TPA-HC for biological visualization of Cu2+ ions. This study establishes a quantitative validation of a turn-ON molecular fluorescence platform for determining trace levels of Cu2+, with real-water analysis and smartphone-assisted screening.
